claims.claim: The acquired image shows Microsoft Visual Basic 4.0.
claims.evidence: Host caption 'Microsoft Visual Basic 4.0 32 bit - Edit' on WinWorld's VB 4.0 product page; in-image title bar 'Loan - Microsoft Visual Basic [design]' and VB 4.0 menu/toolbar layout; sibling About capture from the same session reads 'Microsoft Visual Basic Version 4.0'.

Sibling capture 'Microsoft Visual Basic 4.0 32 bit - About' reads 'For 32-bit Windows Development' on the same Windows 95 desktop with the same window arrangement and a clock two minutes earlier (10:41 PM vs 10:43 PM). The 16-bit About capture reads 'For 16-bit Windows Development' on Windows 3.1. Caveat recorded: the Edit image alone would not prove bitness, because the 16-bit edition also ran on Windows 95.

claims.claim: The image contains the panels XTRA-05 needs: form designer, toolbox, properties window, code window, project window.
claims.evidence: All five visible in source/original.png: toolbox (left), LoanSheet form designer (centre-left, partly covered), Project window 'Loan' (top right), 'Properties - LoanSheet' (bottom right), LoanSheet code window (bottom centre).

claims.claim: SCRIPT.md:132 layout: toolbox on the left, form in the center, properties on the right, code window behind.
claims.evidence: Toolbox is left, the form is centre-left, Properties is right. In this capture the Code window is open in front of the form rather than behind it, which is a state of this session, not a contradiction of the narration. The form here is a populated sample, not the 'blank gray window' of a new project; the sibling 32-bit About capture shows a blank Form1 in the same layout.

claims.claim: SCRIPT.md:130 callout label 'Project Explorer' names the VB4 panel.
claims.evidence: The VB4 capture titles the panel with the project name ('Loan') and shows View Form / View Code buttons; no 'Project Explorer' label appears. Microsoft KB Q136399 ('INFO: Visual Basic and Source Code Control Glyphs', applies to Visual SourceSafe 4.0-6.0, last modified 07-DEC-2001) says: 'In Visual Basic, the Project window displays a list of all the form modules, class modules, and standard modules in the project...'. That supports 'Project window' as Microsoft's term but is not VB4-specific documentation. A search summary claimed Microsoft renamed it to 'Project Explorer' between versions 4 and 5, but the cited thread did not contain that statement, so no primary source for the rename was found. No edit made to War/SCRIPT.md.
claims.proposed_change: For the Writing Lead: change the SCRIPT.md:130 callout 'Project Explorer' to 'Project window' (the VB4-era label), or keep 'Project Explorer' if the video accepts later (VB5/VB6) terminology. Affects XTRA-05 callout text.

claims.claim: ASSET_PLAN.md:89: VB 4.0 IDE screenshots 'exist on Wikipedia' / Wikimedia Commons.
claims.evidence: No VB 4.0 IDE screenshot found on Wikimedia Commons or in the English Wikipedia Visual Basic (classic) article on 2026-09-15; the Wikipedia VB 6.0 screenshot is a non-free local file. Planning-lead note only; ASSET_PLAN.md is hash-locked and needs no script change.
